judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The image is a news-teaser thumbnail that is not inside a link (live markup: div.Teaser_cover-wrapper > img, then a separate h3 headline link whose aria-label is the same headline); its alt repeats the headline word for word. The crop shows an Aldi store sign; the alt speaks of an opening date being announced ten years after planning, which the picture does not show (only the Aldi brand overlaps), so the claim holds of the capture. The live page (fetched 2026-11-25) has the same teaser, img src and alt, so the capture does not differ. Whether this fails 1.1.1 is a point competent auditors split on: read by G94 the photo is informative and the headline does not present what it shows, and if it is taken as eye-candy it should have a null alt (F38's test); but many auditors treat a headline alt on a teaser photo as an alternative that identifies the story, merely redundant with the adjacent link (a best-practice issue, as in axe's image-redundant-alt). My lean is a failure, but reasonable disagreement makes the label uncertain.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The account button in the header shows only an SVG person-in-circle outline; its name comes from aria-label and it has no visible text, border or fill of its own (live CSS: .Avatar_avatar-container background transparent, border none). Live token CSS for the 1280px width (xl-v2.css) sets the strokes to --color-com-header-primary-nav-avatar-bg #ffffff and the header (.Header_header-primary) to #22af9e; #ffffff on #22af9e is 2.73:1, which I recomputed. The icon is the only visual information that identifies the control, so 1.4.11 asks for 3:1 against the adjacent teal and it fails. The full-page screenshot does not show the header at that position (no teal rows there), but Rampa's pixel measurement agrees with the live styles, so the difference does not touch this claim. The claim names the failure: true positive.
